heading: As networks grow, test error can fall, peak near exact training fits, then fall.
definition: as model size grows, test error falls, peaks near the size that just fits the training set, then falls again.
summary: The pattern appears in some experiments that vary network width and depends on training conditions and the evaluation metric, so its generality is contested. Networks trained without label noise can improve monotonically across interpolation, the point where a model fits the training data exactly.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/small-task settings and <1B: C for unqualified V1, alongside reproduced conditional width effects. 1–10B: ? for the complete model-size claim; R0 for the Qwen LoRA peak/recovery observation on a fixed pretrained architecture. 10–100B and >100B: ?; no named-size coverage. Most linked studies have unstated sizes.
suggested_status.reason: C rests on tested failures of the unqualified pattern: clean-label MNIST FCNN test error decreases monotonically across the reported interpolation threshold in arXiv:2310.13572#r1. Clean-label DeiT-Tiny rank sweeps and the short-budget arm warrant challenges, not limits_scope: arXiv:2610.04507#R2 and arXiv:2610.04507#R22 lack the claimed shape over their sampled ranges; clean-label NLL keeps rising across interpolating ranks. Conditional reproduction is explicit in arXiv:2202.11749#R1, with arXiv:2202.11749#R2 supplying the training-fit threshold. The initialization-protocol artifact in arXiv:2211.10322#r6 and arXiv:2211.10322#r7 concerns one-hidden-layer MNIST networks; it supplies no direct deep-architecture failure and receives no V1 verdict. arXiv:2610.04507#R6 extends trainable-capacity evidence to Qwen2.5-7B, rather than establishing dense pretraining size scaling. counts: versions.V1.verdicts records supporting, limiting and challenging evidence; versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size show <1B and 1-10B coverage, no 10-100B or >100B entries, and substantial unstated-size coverage. Author-group independence cannot be established from absent header flags.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched replications controlling architecture, metric, initialization, training duration, regularization and checkpoint selection would clarify the clean-label disagreements and peak alignment. Dense language-model sweeps should report absolute held-out loss and measured full-training-set fit. Deep-architecture reuse-switch interventions would test the artifact's reach. These results could separate a reproducible conditional width phenomenon from the unqualified V1 statement.

source.title: Deep double descent: where bigger models and more data hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

original_result.setup: The original study varied ResNet18 width on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using Adam.
original_result.result: After 4K training epochs on CIFAR-10 with 15% label noise, test error peaked near interpolation and declined as width increased further. With augmentation and no added label noise, CIFAR-100 showed a peak, while CIFAR-10 showed a plateau.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.issue: Width, depth and adapter rank require distinct conditions. Infinite-width CNTKs interpolate at every tested depth but risk rises beyond a critical depth. Interpolating LeNet/MLP/ResNet depth sweeps can stagnate or worsen. Randomly sampled zero-training-error networks lack width improvement in some conditions; another condition improves slightly before stagnating. Self-supervised nonlinear autoencoder width sweeps reach interpolation without the claimed curve. DeiT-Tiny adapter-rank sweeps change trainable capacity within a fixed pretrained architecture; clean-label and short-budget conditions lack the claimed shape.

Clean CIFAR-10 LeNet-like CNNs show an NLL peak while classification accuracy improves through the interpolation region. Small cross-entropy networks show a pronounced population-loss peak but only a slight peak in validation-selected classification error. DeepSurv concordance recovers while integrated Brier score lacks a second descent; its 90%-censoring condition reports no significant double descent. The absent classification-error peak and absent Brier-score recovery are contrary results in their specified metric conditions.

Clean-label FCNN/MNIST test error decreases through the stated interpolation threshold. The CNN study also reports monotonically decreasing generalization error, but its measured training-fit onsets are algorithmic LE thresholds using an at-most-one-misclassified-training-pattern criterion; they do not establish crossing an information-theoretic interpolation threshold. Per-width regularization tuning in WideResNet/DenseNet removes the claimed shape. Other linked results establish only the post-interpolation decline, without the initial descent or peak.

wording_issues.phrase: near the size that just fits the training set
wording_issues.issue: In ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 with label noise, the test-error peak precedes zero training error. DeiT-Tiny adapter-rank sweeps can peak after the first sampled interpolating capacity. Dense pair-label-noise Siamese MLP/CNN sweeps retain a peak while training error stays nonzero, providing only partial V1 evidence. Best-checkpoint DeepONets instead place a minimum near interpolation. The records supply no common tolerance for near.

The second descent can reverse at larger widths. Noisy-label sweeps show final ascent under stronger L2, asymmetric noise or reduced sample fractions. Fixed non-negligible L2 produces large-width deterioration in MNIST MLPs and CIFAR-10 ResNets. CNN-VEC with NTK parameterization loses accuracy at large widths.

A sampled size sweep need not contain a first-fit transition. Bayesian deep-linear width sweeps can interpolate throughout the sampled range. In the noisy-label ViT experiment, trained for 60,000 steps, exact interpolation is not reached; CIFAR-10 supplies ID evaluation and CIFAR-100 supplies OOD evaluation. The ViT result is partial for V1's interpolation requirement.

method_sensitivity.what: The MLP without label noise has no test-error peak; with 15% label noise, error peaks near 50 hidden neurons at interpolation and then decreases. Autoencoder contamination and domain shift change peak presence and recovery: V1 is absent at 0–20% sample noise, and shifts 0.1 and 0.5 lack nonmonotonicity. Quantum-state sample selection changes peak alignment; in the paramagnetic condition, the test-loss peak does not coincide with the training-loss minimum, giving only partial agreement with V1. These findings do not establish added noise as universally necessary.

Small-network interpolation relations differ between MSE and cross-entropy. In the noise-free classification sweep, NLL peaks while accuracy improves through the interpolation region; the accuracy condition challenges V1. Survival concordance can recover while integrated Brier score has no second descent. The survival condition with 90% censoring also lacks significant double descent. Clean CIFAR-100 shows double descent in test loss but explicitly lacks it in classification error; the test-loss result alone cannot determine V1's classification-error effect. The two-spirals test-error sweeps also report absence.

Per-size tuning mitigates or removes nonmonotonicity in dense vision and pretraining sweeps. The jointly tuned pretraining size sweep decreases monotonically, so V1 is absent; its interpolation threshold is not established. Fixed stronger L2 can instead cause final ascent. In ViT pruning, λ=1 at ε=10% removes sparse double descent, and λ=3 at ε=50% produces monotonic performance; these conditions challenge V1 while supporting V6's regularization-removal component. At λ=1 and ε=50%, the peak is mitigated but persists, giving limits_scope. Prescribed theorem curves also depend on regularization policy.

Longer training can reveal optimization-hidden peaks: the extension is 10x for the other displayed slow settings and 16x for full-batch curves. Early stopping or best-epoch evaluation can remove peaks or weaken them. DeepONet best-error and endpoint-averaged curves differ; under high-variance training-label noise, best-loss evaluation has no second-descent advantage. Particle-physics checkpoint selection uses the test set. Its final-checkpoint curves support V1 even when the second descent does not beat the classical minimum.

method_sensitivity.factor: Capacity axis, parameterization and interpolator selection
method_sensitivity.what: Widening and deepening can have opposite post-interpolation effects: infinite-width CNTK risk increases beyond a critical depth despite interpolation at every tested depth. SGD-selected interpolators improve with width, whereas randomly sampled zero-error networks show absent improvement in some conditions and slight improvement followed by stagnation in another. CNN-VEC differs under standard and NTK parameterizations. For the self-supervised nonlinear autoencoder on synthetic Gaussian data at SNR 10, both latent-width and hidden-width sweeps lack the predicted model-wise curve despite reaching interpolation.

Individual predictors improve beyond the transition while ensemble accuracy can stop improving; the reported accuracy improvement alone does not establish a transition-region test-error peak. For ensembles of 5-layer FC nets on binary 10-PCA CIFAR-10, the post-threshold curve flattens at α=100 but dips and then rises at α=10. SWAG mitigates the SGD peak; MultiSWAG removes double descent and gives monotonic width improvement. Mutual learning suppresses and shifts the CNN peak while retaining double descent.

WideResNet-28 on CIFAR-10 with a PGD-10 adversary exhibits width-wise double descent with ReLU but not SiLU; the SiLU condition challenges V1. As shallow-network context, the MNIST initialization switch coincides with the interpolation transition, so it does not distinguish their effects. The same-initialization CIFAR cat/dog experiment reports only a second descent, with no first descent, supplying a partial shape. These one-hidden-layer initialization experiments do not directly test V1's deep-network scope.

Self-adaptive target correction removes the ERM width peak. For MNIST, self-concatenation preserves double descent in validation cross-entropy loss versus parameter count, whereas concatenating different inputs removes that loss peak. These loss measurements do not establish the corresponding classification-error behavior. Different-input CIFAR constructions mitigate ResNet-18 peaks. Concatenated-input ResNet-34 retains a test-error bump at a shifted width; displacement alone does not establish attenuation or incomplete double descent.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task, data quantity and external evaluation
method_sensitivity.what: More arithmetic training samples weaken or remove the size-wise dip. Atari environments and game mixtures produce different depth curves. EEG development error rises from ConvNeXt Nano to Small and falls for larger models, establishing only a partial shape. External EEG evaluation shows a weaker dip across unspecified metrics; the error-rate effect cannot be determined, and late-EEG deterioration beyond Medium concerns MCC. LoRA model-family changes can reverse post-interpolation trends. Clean-label and short-budget DeiT-Tiny rank sweeps lack the claimed shape over their sampled ranges and challenge V1.

method_sensitivity.factor: Diffusion training-noise construction and diffusion time
method_sensitivity.what: Changing sample count and fixed noise-realization count moves the CelebA U-Net peak with interpolation. Its second-descent plateau rises at smaller diffusion time. The CIFAR10 diffusion study reports no second descent under a different setup.
